change.title: pr-37429-flat
change.description: Add HTML sanitizer for translated message resources
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Account UI message switched from i18next `{{n}}` placeholders to MessageFormat syntax that i18next won't interpolate
findings.body: This bundle is loaded by i18next, and `js/apps/account-ui/src/i18n.ts:27-29` sets no custom interpolation prefix, so the default `{{ }}` delimiters apply. Every sibling error message in this file uses `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` (lines 14, 27, 29, 36, 37). The new value uses `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and a Java `{2,choice,...}` pattern, and i18next interpolates none of these. A user who breaks a multivalued size constraint in the Account Console would see the literal text `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` The same change is in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138`, so the Admin Console has the same problem. Keep the `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` form for the two React bundles, for example `... at most {{2}} value(s).`, or use i18next plurals. Apply the MessageFormat `choice` form only to the server-rendered themes. I did not read the ui-shared code that passes `error.params` to `t()`, which is why confidence is medium.

findings.title: Admin UI message now uses MessageFormat placeholders that i18next won't substitute
findings.body: This is the same problem as in the account-ui bundle. The old value used the i18next `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` placeholders, which the React admin console interpolates. The new value uses `{0}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, which i18next leaves as literal text, so admins would see raw placeholders in the validation error. Keep i18next syntax in this bundle.

findings.title: Anchor violation message names neither the key nor the file
findings.body: `ThemeVerifierMojo` collects the messages from every scanned properties file into one list and throws `MojoFailureException("Validation errors: " + messages)` (`misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/ThemeVerifierMojo.java:51-55`). The duplicate-key message (line 194) and the illegal-HTML message (line 111) both include the file, and the HTML one includes the key. This message has only the tag, so with dozens of locale files a failing build gives no clue which translation to fix. Add `key` (the parameter is already passed in but never used) and `file` to the message.

findings.title: ANCHOR_PATTERN also matches `<abbr>`, `<area>`, `<audio>`, `<address>` …
findings.body: `</?a[^>]*>` matches any tag whose name starts with `a`. Nothing unsafe gets through: an unmatched tag is still reported. But a translation containing `<abbr>` or `<audio …>` is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" instead of as illegal HTML, which is misleading. `</?a(\s[^>]*)?>` limits the match to real anchors.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException
findings.body: Line 74 derives the English file path by string rewriting. If a scanned messages file has no `_en` sibling at that path (a theme that only ships translations, or a different directory layout), `verifySafeHtml` throws an unchecked `RuntimeException`. The mojo does not catch it, so it ends the build with a stack trace and no aggregated report. `verify()` already converts I/O errors to `MojoExecutionException`. Either do the same here, or fall back to treating every English value as "no HTML".

contracts.action: The theme verifier now loads each messages file and its English counterpart and sanitizes each value with the OWASP HTML sanitizer
contracts.equivalent_path: verifyNoDuplicateKeys, called from verify() and aggregated by ThemeVerifierMojo
contracts.before_after: verifyNoDuplicateKeys reports through the messages list and includes the file path. verifySafeHtml includes key and file for illegal HTML, but its anchor message (line 157) has neither.
contracts.visible_effect: The mojo concatenates all messages into one MojoFailureException, and that is the build failure developers see.
contracts.failure_mode: If the English sibling file is missing, a RuntimeException ends the build without the aggregated report. An anchor mismatch produces a message that cannot be traced to a key or file.

contracts.action: error-invalid-multivalued-size changed to the MessageFormat choice syntax in the server themes and in the React UI bundles
contracts.equivalent_path: The other validation messages in the same bundle use i18next `{{n}}` placeholders
contracts.before_after: Server side, MultiValueValidator passes Long min/max as params, so `{2,choice,...}` formats correctly in the FreeMarker/MessageFormat themes. The React bundles previously used `{{n}}` like their siblings.
contracts.visible_effect: The Account and Admin consoles would show the raw `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` text in the validation error.
contracts.failure_mode: The broken placeholders show up silently in the UI, with no error.
contracts.open_question: Does ui-shared pass error.params to i18next `t()` so that `{{n}}` is the only syntax interpolated?

summary: The PR adds an OWASP-sanitizer-based HTML check to the theme verifier and fixes the translations it flags. Main concern: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in the account-ui and admin-ui React bundles was switched from the i18next `{{n}}` placeholders to Java MessageFormat `{n}`/`choice` syntax. i18next doesn't interpolate that, so the consoles would likely show raw placeholders. In the verifier itself, the anchor-mismatch message names neither the key nor the file, which makes failures hard to trace. Smaller points: ANCHOR_PATTERN is over-broad, a missing English sibling file aborts the build with an unchecked exception, and one test fixture is malformed.
